canvas-01-1.description: Sheet 1 of the September 1924 Sanborn atlas of the Borough of Linwood covers the middle of the borough on both sides of Shore Road, which runs along the bottom of the sheet. North of Shore Road the sheet shows Poplar Avenue running up to the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (Shore Fast Line, electric and steam) and on to Oak Grove Avenue and Maple Avenue, with Rena Street meeting Maple Avenue near the top. East of Poplar, the platted blocks of Wilson, Davis, Barr and Haines Avenues run from Shore Road up to Irwin Avenue, divided into narrow lots that are almost all still vacant. The built-up frontage is thin: frame dwellings and outbuildings along Shore Road, Poplar Avenue and Maple Avenue, poultry houses on the larger lots, the Linwood Borough Hall on Poplar Avenue, the Masonic Hall south of Shore Road, Margaret Villa, and the Linwood Poultry Farm. South of Shore Road the land belongs to the Linwood Country Club golf links. Water pipes of 4 to 10 inches are marked in the streets. The upper right of the sheet carries the atlas title, the water and fire department report, the key, the street index and a key map of the whole borough at 1200 feet to an inch; these are cut out of this part. A boxed inset of the Linwood Country Club buildings at the bottom is a separate part that could not be placed. The scale is 100 feet to an inch.
notes: Irwin Avenue is now Lincoln Avenue.
Rena Street (marked arbitrary in the index) is now Edna Avenue.
Linwood Borough Hall on Poplar Avenue; Masonic Hall south of Shore Road.
Index lists 7 sheets; population 1000.

Sheet 1, 100 ft. Map with the title, water/fire report, key, index and 1200 ft key map in a panel at upper right (cut out of the mask) and a boxed inset of the Linwood Country Club buildings (no exposure, no streets) at bottom. Shore Rd along the bottom; Poplar, Wilson, Davis, Barr, Haines Avs; Irwin Av (now Lincoln Avenue), Rena St (now Edna Avenue), Maple, Oak Grove. Part 1 configured; part 2 (country club inset) not placed.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Linwood Country Club buildings (boxed, 'no exposure any side') (no street junction or other feature shared with the modern data; needs position of the 1924 clubhouse (e.g. from an aerial) as hand-picked control; step 6b).

sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 covers the north end of Linwood at the boundary with the City of Northfield, which is drawn as a dash-dot line between Vernon and Oakcrest Avenues with the note 'See Map of Northfield'. Shore Road crosses the bottom of the sheet; above it Central Avenue runs diagonally north-west across the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (Shore Fast Line, electric and steam), which crosses the middle of the sheet. North of the railroad, Wabash Avenue runs along the track and a grid of Marvin, Vernon and Oakcrest Avenues crossed by Fenton and Warren Avenues is laid out in narrow lots, with scattered frame dwellings, poultry houses and sheds. South of the railroad Marvin Avenue continues to Shore Road, where the Central M.E. Church stands near the corner of Central Avenue, and a cemetery lies on the south side of Shore Road. Haines Avenue meets Shore Road at the left edge, matching sheet 1. Most of the west half of the sheet is open land, and the Linwood Country Club golf links occupy the land south of Shore Road. The scale is 100 feet to an inch.
notes: Central M.E. Church on Shore Road at Central Avenue; cemetery opposite.
Vernon Avenue is now West Vernon Avenue north of Shore Road and East Vernon Avenue south of it; Oakcrest Avenue is West Oakcrest Avenue.
Fenton Avenue has no modern counterpart in the reference data.
The fitted scale is about 2.5 percent larger than on sheets 1 and 3.

100 ft. North end at the Northfield line: Shore Rd, Haines, Central, Marvin, Vernon, Warren, Oakcrest, Fenton, Wabash Avs; railroad (W.J.&S.R.R. Shore Fast Line). Drawn scale fits about 2.5 percent larger than sheets 1 and 3.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 covers the centre of Linwood around the railroad station. Shore Road runs along the bottom of the sheet and the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (Shore Fast Line) across the middle. Maple Avenue runs diagonally from Shore Road to the railroad, crossing Elm Avenue; along it stand the post office, stores and dwellings, and near the track the Linwood station and the warehouse of the Linwood Farmers Supplies. North of the railroad, Oak Grove Avenue and Wabash Avenue follow the track, Oak Avenue or Bog Road runs diagonally across the top, and the platted streets Ireland, Tabor, Oak Lane, Sanders, Adams and Van Sant Avenues run between them, with Short Street between Sanders and Adams; the blocks are cut into narrow lots with a few dwellings and a water tower. South of the railroad Ireland and Tabor Avenues are marked not opened. Maple and Elm Avenues continue south of Shore Road. The scale is 100 feet to an inch.
notes: Adams Avenue is now Jefferson Avenue; Sanders Avenue is now West Edgewood Avenue; Oak Lane is now West Monroe Avenue; Ireland Avenue is now West Essex Avenue (north of Shore Road) and East Essex Avenue (south).
Oak Grove Avenue west of Van Sant Avenue is now part of Wabash Avenue.
Tabor Avenue south of the railroad is on the line of modern Glenside Avenue.
Linwood station, Linwood Farmers Supplies warehouse and the post office on Maple Avenue.

100 ft. Shore Rd, Maple, Elm, Van Sant, Oak Grove/Wabash (north of rail), Oak Av or Bog Rd, Adams (now Jefferson Avenue), Sanders (now West Edgewood Avenue), Oak Lane (now West Monroe Avenue), Tabor, Ireland (now West/East Essex Avenue). Linwood station and post office.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 covers the land between Ireland Avenue and Walnut Avenue on both sides of Shore Road, which runs along the lower part of the sheet. The West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (Shore Fast Line) crosses the middle. Oak Avenue or Bog Road crosses the railroad diagonally and meets West Avenue or Bethel Road and Belhaven Avenue at a small triangle, beside which stands the Linwood Public School. Belhaven Avenue and Essex Place run from Shore Road towards the school; Osee Court is laid out north of the railroad; Grant Avenue appears at the left edge. South of Shore Road, Walnut Avenue and Elmwood Avenue are drawn as streets marked not opened. Most of the sheet is large undivided tracts with a few dwellings, outbuildings and stores. The scale is 100 feet to an inch.
notes: Linwood Public School at Belhaven Avenue and West Avenue.
West Avenue or Bethel Road north-west of Belhaven Avenue no longer exists on this line.
Elmwood Avenue (not opened in 1924) is on the line of modern Ireland Avenue; the 1924 Ireland Avenue is modern Essex Avenue.
Walnut Avenue, Essex Place and Osee Court have no modern counterpart in the reference data.

100 ft. Shore Rd, Belhaven, West Av or Bethel Rd (old alignment, gone), Oak Av, Ireland (now Essex), Elmwood Av not opened (now Ireland Avenue), Walnut, Essex Pl, Osee Ct. Linwood Public School. Few surviving junctions; detector found 2, rest hand-picked.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 covers the land between Seaview Avenue and Patcong Avenue on both sides of Shore Road, which runs across the lower part of the sheet. The West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (Shore Fast Line) crosses above it, and West Avenue or Bethel Road runs diagonally from the upper left to the railroad near Patcong Avenue. In the upper right a platted block between Hamilton and Patcong Avenues is divided by Grant Avenue and bounded by Adams Avenue, marked not opened, with narrow lots and a few dwellings. Asbury Avenue is a short street north of Shore Road with dwellings on both sides, and Gray Gables is named on Seaview Avenue. The rest of the sheet is long narrow farm lots and large tracts with dwellings along Shore Road, hen houses and a store; the land south of Shore Road is marked vacant beyond. The scale is 100 feet to an inch.
notes: Seaview Avenue is now West Seaview Avenue north of Shore Road; Patcong Avenue is West and East Patcong Avenue.
Hamilton Avenue did not reach Shore Road in 1924.
West Avenue or Bethel Road at Hamilton Avenue lies about 10 m from the modern West Avenue junction; it was not used as control.
100 ft. Shore Rd, Seaview, Asbury, Patcong, Hamilton, Grant, Adams, West Av or Bethel Rd. Mostly large tracts. All control hand-picked (detector locked onto lot lines).

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 covers the south-central part of Linwood between Seaview Avenue and the boundary with sheet 7, on both sides of Shore Road. The West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (Shore Fast Line, electric and steam) crosses the upper part of the sheet, with the Sea View station and freight depot at Seaview Avenue. Garfield Avenue runs from the railroad to Shore Road, lined with dwellings on narrow lots; Iona Avenue runs south from Shore Road between narrow lots. Seaview Avenue jogs at Shore Road. Along Shore Road stand dwellings, several named cottages (Goldenrod, The Gazelle, Sunset Cottage, Edna May, Haven Hedge, Mistletoe, Hollywood) and the Seaview Baptist Church. North of the railroad and south of Shore Road the land is mostly large tracts and long farm lots; the bottom right is marked vacant beyond. The sheet has a 'Scale of Feet' bar in place of the usual one; the scale is 100 feet to an inch.
notes: Sea View station and freight depot of the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad.
Seaview Baptist Church on Shore Road.
Seaview Avenue is offset at Shore Road: West Seaview Avenue north, East Seaview Avenue south.
100 ft (separate 'Scale of Feet' bar). Shore Rd, Garfield, Iona, Seaview (offset at Shore: West Seaview north, East Seaview south). Sea View station and freight depot.

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 covers the south end of Linwood at the boundary with the City of Somers Point, which runs along Ocean Heights Avenue and down the left side of the sheet with the note 'See Map of Somers Point'. Shore Road crosses the middle of the sheet and the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (Shore Fast Line) the top. Between them a subdivision of narrow lots is laid out along Princess and Victoria Avenues and Royal Avenue, mostly vacant. South of Shore Road, Royal Avenue and Drury Lane run down through further platted blocks crossed by Chatham and Laurel Avenues, which are marked not opened, towards the salt meadows; the line of the meadows is drawn across the lower part. The Colonial Green House buildings stand south of Shore Road near Ocean Heights Avenue, and a fire alarm box is marked at the corner. The right half of the sheet is large tracts with a few dwellings and two lanes. The scale is 100 feet to an inch.
notes: Drury Lane is on the line of modern East Ocean Heights Avenue.
Princess, Victoria, Chatham and Laurel Avenues were not opened; the modern Victoria Avenue is a different street.
Colonial Green House on Shore Road.

100 ft. South end at the Somers Point line: Shore Rd, Ocean Heights Av, Royal Av, Princess, Victoria, Chatham, Laurel (not opened), Drury Lane (now East Ocean Heights Avenue), Colonial Green House, salt meadows. Only two junctions survive (both on Shore Rd): helmert.
